Republican incumbent [[Jim Jeffords]] was re-elected to a third term over Democratic [[Vermont State Auditor|state auditor]] [[Ed Flanagan (politician)|Ed Flanagan]] in a [[Landslide victory|landslide]]. {{As of|2026}}, this is the Vermont federal election won by a Republican and the last time that either party won this seat.{{efn|[[Bernie Sanders]], who replaced Jeffords in the 2006 election, is an [[Independent politician|independent]] who caucuses with the Democrats, like Jeffords did during his final term.}} In May 2001, Jeffords left the Republican Party, became an independent, and joined the Democratic Party caucus in the Senate. His switch broke the 50–50 deadlock in the Senate and gave the Democrats the majority. The switch marked the first time since the foundation of the Republican Party circa 1855 that Vermont had no Republicans in its congressional delegation. == Republican primary == === Candidates === * Russell (Constitution) ====Declined==== *[[Bernie Sanders]], U.S. representative and former mayor of [[Burlington, Vermont|Burlington]]{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2000/10/05/politics/senator-jeffords-on-firm-ground-for-reelection-bid.html|title=Senator Jeffords on Firm Ground for Re-election Bid|newspaper=The New York Times|date=October 5, 2006|accessdate=July 19, 2021}} (Independent) === Campaign === Flanagan was widely seen as having little chance of beating the highly popular Jeffords, who was thought of as a [[Rockefeller Republican|liberal Republican]].{{cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2000/ALLPOLITICS/stories/11/02/vermont.senate/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010509082203/http://edition.cnn.com/2000/ALLPOLITICS/stories/11/02/vermont.senate/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 9, 2001|title=Gay Senate candidate an underdog amid Vermont gay union backlash|website=CNN|last1=Delaney|first1=Bill|date=November 2, 2000|accessdate=July 19, 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/2000/07/24/gay-official-aims-to-shake-up-senate/807be4c6-f7da-4d02-b250-b2640404514e/|title=Gay Official Aims to Shake Up Senate|newspaper=The Washington Post|last1=Ferdin|first1=Pamela|date=July 24, 2000|accessdate=July 19, 2021}} Flanagan campaigned on "shaking up Washington" and portrayed himself as a reformer. Both candidates supported same-sex [[civil unions]] and remained silent on the issue of [[same-sex marriage]], but Flanagan, who was openly gay, noted receiving backlash from voters opposed to same-sex marriage. The [[LGBTQ people|LGBTQ community]] in Vermont was divided between which candidate to support, as Jeffords had been strongly supportive of LGBT rights and received a perfect score from the [[Human Rights Campaign]]. ===Endorsements=== {{Endorsements box | title = Jim Jeffords (R) | list = '''Organizations''' *[[Sierra Club]]{{cite web|url=http://fbaum.unc.edu/lobby/_107th/126_CAFE_Standards_2/Organizational_Statements/SC/SC_Leaders_Wanted.htm|title=Leaders Wanted|website=Sierra Club|date=August 2000|accessdate=July 19, 2021}} *[[U.S. Chamber of Commerce]]{{cite web|url=https://www.uschamber.com/press-release/us-chamber-announces-latest-political-endorsements|title=U.S. Chamber Announces Latest of Political Endorsements|website=U.S. Chamber of Commerce|date=May 7, 2000|accessdate=July 19, 2021|format=Press release|archive-date=July 11, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210711113450/https://www.uschamber.com/press-release/us-chamber-announces-latest-political-endorsements|url-status=dead}} }} === Polling === {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign="bottom" ! scope="col" |Poll source ! scope="col" |Date(s) ! scope="col" style="width:75px;" |Sample
